_about: Literature reference values for results/llif/scripts/build_cadaveric_validation_table.py. Every number below was checked on 2026-09-28 against the source named in its `verified_against` field; `verification_level` says whether that was the primary paper itself or a secondary paper reproducing it. Numbers whose primary could not be reached are marked `secondary_reproduction` and still need a check against the primary PDF before publication.

panjabi1992.citation: Panjabi MM, Goel V, Oxland T, Takata K, Duranceau J, Krag M, Price M. Human lumbar vertebrae. Quantitative three-dimensional anatomy. Spine. 1992;17(3):299-306.
panjabi1992.design_verified_against: primary full text (user-supplied scanned PDF, 2026-09-28), p. 299 Methods: 'Twelve fresh autopsy spine specimens (axis to last lumbar vertebra)'; mean age 46.3 (19-59) y; male/female 8/4; soft tissue completely removed; 3D morphometer; Table 2 footnote '*Mean +/- SEM'

tan2002.citation: Tan SH, Teo EC, Chua HC. Quantitative three-dimensional anatomy of lumbar vertebrae in Singaporean Asians. Eur Spine J. 2002;11:152-158.
tan2002.design_verified_against: primary abstract (Europe PMC): '60 lumbar vertebrae from 12 cadavers'; 'means and standard errors'

berry1987.citation: Berry JL, Moran JM, Berg WS, Steffee AD. A morphometric study of human lumbar and selected thoracic vertebrae. Spine. 1987;12(4):362-367.
berry1987.design_verified_against: primary abstract (Europe PMC): 'prepared spinal columns from 30 skeletons belonging to the Hamann-Todd Osteological Collection'
berry1987.dispersion_note: abstract does not say SD vs SEM, so no standardized difference is computed against Berry

weinberg2016.citation: Weinberg DS, Morris WZ, Gebhart JJ, Liu RW. Pelvic incidence: an anatomic investigation of 880 cadaveric specimens. Eur Spine J. 2016;25(11):3589-3595.
weinberg2016.specimen: dry bone (Hamann-Todd Osteological Collection), reconstructed pelvis
weinberg2016.dispersion_note: abstract reports '46.0 +/- 11.0' without naming it; with n=880 a +/-11 deg SEM is impossible, so it is SD

can2024.citation: Can H, Ozturk O, Civelek E, Dogu H, Boyali O, Kucuk C, Aydoseli A, Sencer A. A Morphometric Study of Cadavers for the Anterior Approach to the Lower Lumbar Spine. Turk Neurosurg. 2024;34(4):640-646.
can2024.design_verified_against: primary abstract (Europe PMC): '13 fresh human cadavers'; 'presented as mean and standard deviation'

pluemvitayaporn2025.citation: Pluemvitayaporn T, Tadee S, Kunakornsawat S, et al. What Is the Suitable Wide Cage Size for Stand-alone LLIF in Asian Population: A Computed Tomography Scan-Based Study of a Dimension of Lumbar Endplate. Asian J Neurosurg. 2025;20(1):119-125.
pluemvitayaporn2025.specimen: CT, living patients (NOT cadaveric; same-modality comparator)
pluemvitayaporn2025.design_verified_against: primary full text (Europe PMC): 91 CT scans, 52 M / 39 F, 'mean and standard deviation (SD)'; IVDH = 'maximum distance of the intervertebral disc'

references.comparability_note: bony dimension; our value is the bounding-box width of the segmented, body-isolated endplate surface

values.verified_against: Panjabi 1992 Table 2, p. 301 (EPWl, L4); matches PMC11875720 Table 2 reproduction (which rounds the SEM)
Panjabi 1992 Table 2, p. 301 (EPDl, L4); matches PMC11875720 Table 2 reproduction (which rounds the SEM)
Panjabi 1992 Table 2, p. 301 (EPWu, L5); matches PMC11875720 Table 2 reproduction (which rounds the SEM)
Panjabi 1992 Table 2, p. 301 (EPDu, L5); matches PMC11875720 Table 2 reproduction (which rounds the SEM)

references.comparability_note: bony dimension; ours is the superior-inferior gap between the body's own posterior endplate corners
bony dimension; ours is the superior-inferior gap between the body's own posterior endplate corners
morphological, posture-independent; dry-bone reconstruction vs. our CT femoral-head/sacral-endplate fit
post-mortem discs lose water/height and were measured directly on the exposed anterior surface; agreement here does NOT validate our disc height
same modality (CT), living patients; their IVDH is the 'maximum distance of the intervertebral disc' on sagittal CT, so we compare our max of ant/mid/post

not_referenced.vertebral rotation, lateral listhesis, s: patient-specific and/or posture-dependent -- no meaningful cadaveric reference exists.
not_referenced.vertebral HU: post-mortem/fixation changes attenuation; cadaveric HU is not a reference for living-patient CT.
not_referenced.L4/L5 anterior vertebral body height: Panjabi 1992 Table 2 reports posterior height (VBHp) only; no verified cadaveric anterior-height reference yet.
